---
title: "Titles"
---

`dofjson.legal_provisions_titles()` yields a small `codNota`, `titulo`,
`fecha` and `codOrgaUno` record for every legal provision ever published,
sourced from the
[`notas-archivo` GitHub release](https://github.com/legistlan/dofjson/releases/tag/notas-archivo).
`titulo` is Spanish for "title" and `fecha` for "date": `codNota` is what to
fetch the provision's full content with later, `titulo` serves exploratory
analysis of the titles, `fecha` places each title in time, and `codOrgaUno`
groups by issuing branch.

```python
import dofjson

for titulo in dofjson.legal_provisions_titles():
    ...
# titulo == {"codNota": 4434476, "titulo": "CIRCULAR nº. 164, ...",
#            "fecha": "23-03-1917", "codOrgaUno": None}
```

## The release

The release holds one `notas-YYYY.tgz` per closed year, 1917 to last year, and
one `notas-YYYY-MM.tgz` per month of the current year. Each archive holds one
`DDMMYYYY-notas.json` per day, in the same shape [`--archivo`](archive.qmd)
writes. A monthly workflow builds the previous month on the 1st and folds a
closed year into one asset on 1 January.

The release is owned by this repository. The environment variable
`DOFJSON_RELEASE_REPOSITORY` (`<owner>/<name>`) points the lookup at a mirror
of the release held elsewhere, and is read on every call.

Listing the release's assets is one request to the GitHub API, where an
unauthenticated address gets 60 requests an hour. When `GH_TOKEN` (or
`GITHUB_TOKEN`) is set, that request carries it as a bearer token; without one
nothing changes. The asset downloads themselves are outside that quota.

## Downloading the assets

`download_dof_assets` downloads the release into a cache, independently of
reading it. Populate it once and every pass afterwards is local:

```python
from dofjson.titulos import download_dof_assets

download_dof_assets()               # -> dofjson.titulos.CACHE_DIR
download_dof_assets(Path("cache"))  # -> one notas-YYYY[-MM].tgz per asset, here instead
```

Nothing but these assets is written. `cache_dir` resolves the same way
everywhere in the package: left out, it is the package-wide
`dofjson.titulos.CACHE_DIR`; a directory reads that one; and an explicit
`cache_dir=None` skips the disk and downloads every asset straight into memory
(`SIN_CACHE_DIR` is the sentinel that tells "nothing passed" from "skip").

```python
dofjson.legal_provisions_titles(Path("cache"))       # a cache of your own
dofjson.legal_provisions_titles(cache_dir=None)      # nothing on disk
```

The `codOrgaUno` to `nombreCodOrgaUno` map comes out of the same pass:
`dofjson.organigrama()` makes that pass on its own, or pass your own dict as
`organigrama=` to get both at once. The titles stream is not re-iterable: a
second pass re-reads the assets, so call it again or materialize what you need.

## Reading a whole asset, not just titles

`legal_provisions_titles` keeps four fields per titled provision.
`dofjson.notas_de_tgz` is the general form: every field a note carries, in
publication order (by day, then by `codNota` within the day).

```python
for nota in dofjson.notas_de_tgz(Path("cache/notas-1980.tgz").read_bytes()):
    ...  # nota carries every field SIDOF or the website published it with
```

`dofjson.iterador_de_assets` is `notas_de_tgz` over the whole release: it
downloads, or reads from `cache_dir`, every `notas-YYYY[-MM].tgz` in turn and
yields every note across all of them, never holding more than one asset's
notes in memory. `legal_provisions_titles` is built on it.

```python
for nota in dofjson.iterador_de_assets():                # every note ever published
    ...
for nota in dofjson.iterador_de_assets(Path("cache")):   # reuse a cache_dir on disk
    ...
```

## Fewer calls to SIDOF with `cache_dir`

A day's notes index, `dofjson.get_notas(date)`, is exactly what a
`notas-archivo` asset holds for an already-published date. So when a
`cache_dir` populated by `download_dof_assets` has that date, it is read off
disk instead of asking SIDOF or the website at all:

```python
from dofjson import api

api.get_notas(date, cache_dir=Path("cache"))   # a cache hit skips the network entirely
```

Leaving `cache_dir` out still gets the cache, through `CACHE_DIR`; pass
`cache_dir=None` to skip it for just that call. The same default flows through
`dofjson --archivo` and the command line's single-date query:

```bash
dofjson --archivo --cache-dir cache        # a specific directory
dofjson 1980-01-02 --endpoint notas        # no --cache-dir: uses CACHE_DIR
dofjson 1980-01-02 --endpoint notas --cache-dir none  # always fetch live
```

`dofjson.get_nota(codNota)` has no matching `cache_dir`: the archive only ever
holds the daily index, never a provision's own `cadenaContenido`, which always
takes the one-note request `get_nota()` already makes.
